subject: Orbital Health: chat session churn and elevated 5xx/429
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex@orbitalhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Ops Team <ops@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-05T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Chat sessions dropping mid-conversation

Karthik —

We had a major regression in our patient triage assistant this morning. Between 07:40–08:10PT we saw a spike of 5xx and 429 responses from Redwood for streaming chat completions. Clients observed stream disconnects around ~8–12s after the first token and many user sessions immediately retried, which amplified the load. I've attached a trimmed log excerpt.

Impact: several clinicians reported interrupted conversations and a backlog on our message queue. Our uptime dashboard shows a 7% spike in errors and latency P95 jumped from 220ms to 1.6s.

Can someone confirm whether this was a platform incident or a client-side timeout behavior? We need an immediate mitigation and a post-mortem timeline.

—Alex
Director of Ops, Orbital Health

Attachment: orbital_logs_20280505.txt (text, 1.2MB, excerpt)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Monroe <alex@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-05T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Chat sessions dropping mid-conversation

Alex — thanks for the log. I’m taking point.

Quick summary of what we’ll do now:
- Triage live metrics (5xx/429 per model variant, region, and route) — Hannah and I are on it.
- Short-term mitigation: enable route throttling and temporary burst cap to stop retry amplification, then reintroduce graceful 429 backoff headers.
- Ask Orbital to hold client retry aggressiveness (increase client-side backoff) while we stabilize.

Can you confirm your SDK/timeo ut settings? Any recent client deploys?

I’ll route this to ops and loop in Van for exec communications if we need credits or an SLA exception.

—Karthik
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-05T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Chat sessions dropping mid-conversation

Attaching initial metric slices and short notes.

Findings so far (07:30–08:20PT window):
- Elevated 5xx rate concentrated on model: gptx-2-320k (north-virginia): 5xx jumped from baseline 0.3% to 6.8%.
- 429 rate spiked for streaming endpoints (chat.stream) and correlated with a surge of small, concurrent sessions (median seq length small).
- Evidence of retry amplification: ~40% of sessions reopened within 10s of disconnect.
- No CPU/GPU OOMs on our nodes; memory/KV-cache appears stable.

Attachments: slo_latency_graph.png (P95/P99) and a prefiltered error trace.

Recommendation (immediate):
1) Apply a soft circuit-breaker on chat.stream for Orbital’s tenant ID for 30 minutes to break retry loops.
2) Push 429 Retry-After and a jittered backoff header for streaming responses.
3) Ask Orbital to patch their SDK to add exponential client backoff on stream disconnects (we can share a patch).

I’ll keep digging into kernel-level logs.

—Hannah
SRE, Redwood Inference

NOTE: quoting their log: 
"On Fri, May 5, 2028 at 07:48 Alex Monroe <alex@orbitalhealth.com> wrote:
> We saw repeated 5xx and 429s across many clients...
"

Thanks Hannah — we just pushed a client rollback (reverted a streaming timeout change) at 08:55PT which temporarily reduced session churn, but we still saw intermittent disconnects.

We can accept the tenant-specific circuit-breaker for 30 minutes. Please also share the SDK patch and any telemetry flags we should flip.

We’re concerned about user experience during Monday clinic hours — this needs priority attention.

—Alex
